source: 李白《黃鶴樓送孟浩然之廣陵》 (4 verse-lines, Wikisource text of record via corpus/tang_en/zh_source/li_bai_huanghelou_song_menghaoran.txt) ↔ Ezra Pound, Cathay (1915), 'Separation on the River Kiang' (title + 5 body lines, Gutenberg #50155, corpus/tang_en/raw/pound_cathay_1915.txt line 479).

map.note: 故人西辭黃鶴樓 ↔ 'Ko-jin goes west from Ko-kaku-ro,' — 故人/old friend (Ko-jin), 西辭/takes leave westward, 黃鶴樓/the Yellow Crane Tower (Ko-kaku-ro, the Japanese reading Pound follows). NB zh 黃 (yellow, in 黃鶴樓) is a colour graph on L1 — a separate colour crossing, not the target; Pound transliterates the tower name and drops 'yellow'.

煙花三月下揚州 ↔ 'The smoke-flowers are blurred over the river.' — 煙花/mist-flowers (smoke-flowers), 三月/third month, 下揚州/going down to Yangzhou. Pound compresses the season/destination into the smoke-flowers image.

TARGET. 孤帆遠影碧山盡 ↔ 'His lone sail blots the far sky.' — 孤帆/lone sail, 遠影/far shadow, 碧山/jade-green hills (main reading; variants 碧空/緑山), 盡/vanishes. The crossing of interest on the COLOUR axis: zh 碧 (jade-green/azure) STATED-as-graph × Pound 'the far sky' (no explicit hue-word). Clean 1:1 for the target line. Measured honestly (see registration): 碧 does NOT fire the zh WORD colour boolean (it is held latent in the 五色 term set), and 'sky' DOES fire the en word colour, so the crossing is NOT a simple colour loss.

唯見長江天際流 ↔ 'And now I see only the river,' / 'The long Kiang, reaching heaven.' — 唯見/only see, 長江/the long river (the Yangtze / Kiang), 天際流/flowing to the horizon. Pound SPLITS this final zh line across his lines 4 AND 5 (a line-boundary event, declared). Not the target; recorded for completeness. For any crossing on zh L4 the two Pound lines would be JOINED ('And now I see only the river, The long Kiang, reaching heaven.').
